One C++17 function-local static raw pointer runs its initializer only until first success. It validates self-image lookup/path/base and acquires RTLD_LAZY|RTLD_NOLOAD only, refusing null without an alternate path or new-image fallback. Compilation flags retain-std=c++17 and do not disable thread-safe statics. This is language/source reasoning, not a concurrency test or C++ AST compilation.

Handle-specific dlsym names the unique registerAll entry; a second dladdr and exact image-base equality bind the resolved entry to the private anchor image. A path-override success from another loaded image cannot silently satisfy this check. Failed lookup/base mismatch closes only the newly acquired extra handle, then throws; a close error also throws. No registration follows either refusal. Rejected-handle release is attempted and checked, not promised infallible.

Success returns the raw handle into trivial pointer storage with no successful-path dlclose, RAII object, atexit callback, NODELETE or preload. The unchanged Registry::registerObjectsTo call follows only after retention. If later object registration throws, the already successful reference remains retained; this bounded deliberate lifetime extension is the candidate behavior, not hidden cleanup or a cause proof.

A throwing initializer may be attempted again by a later caller under C++ rules; later successful calls reuse the static pointer without another acquire. There is no loop/retry/fallback in the shim and no external retry authority in this preparation. Same-image association is established on first successful initialization; later calls reuse that retained identity.
